newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds tumbled on Wednesday, tracking other European debt markets and a weaker peseta in highly volatile trade.
"It's a very dangerous market, I'd rather stay out. The peseta is the key --everyone was long of pesetas and now they are reversing their position," a dealer in Madrid said.
The peseta ended its trading day in Spain at around 84.60/63 versus the mark, against yesterday's close at 84.40/43.
Meanwhile the long-term debt future was trading 91 basis points down at 113.44, with the next support at around 113.34.
Dealers said tomorrow could bring further fallout.
A stronger German mark was penalising peripheral markets, and the 10-year spread versus Bunds widened to 92 basis points from 86 basis points this morning.
Spain's yield curve flattened slightly. The 9.4-percent April 1999 bond ended at 104.93, yielding 5.43 percent. The spread over the 10-year benchmark was around 131 basis points from 142 on Tuesday.

"The correction at the short end was easier to understand given the weak peseta, but I guess this one is over," a dealer said. "What's really scary is the longer end, which could lose more in the coming days".
